title: Group Airfare vs. Individual Tickets: Which Saves More?
metaDescription: Compare group airfare with buying individual tickets. See when group fares save money, how deposits and name changes work, and when individual tickets win.
content:
If you are organizing a trip for a team, a wedding party or a school group, you will quickly face a choice: request a group fare, or have everyone buy their own ticket? Here is how the two compare.

How group fares are priced

Group fares come from a separate inventory managed by the airline's group desk. The airline quotes one price per seat for the whole party, based on the route, dates, season and group size.

When group fares usually win

  • Large groups on popular routes, where buying many individual seats would push the price up.
  • Trips booked months ahead, when you do not yet know every traveler's name.
  • Groups that need to collect money from many people before paying in full.
  • Travelers who must sit together or share special requirements, such as sports equipment.

When individual tickets can be better

  • Very small groups, where a flash sale fare may undercut the group rate.
  • Trips where travelers depart from many different cities on different days.
  • Last-minute travel, when group desks may have limited space.

Don't forget the hidden value of flexibility

Even when the per-seat price is similar, a group contract's deposit, later name deadline and ability to release unused seats can save real money if plans change.
